speaker: forbess
text: Very good, thank you very much, chair. It's a pleasure to be before you this evening or this afternoon. The first minor variance application that's before you by Mr. Claude Perreault deals with lands described as lot, 43 King Street in Montague. The planning report that's been presented to you identifies the location of the subject lands and that it is in the general residential dash two zone. The first application is to have a modest, or is requesting a modest reduction in the minimum lot size that's set out for the R2 or RG-2 zone. Currently, the bylaw requires 665 square meters of minimum lot size. And the proposal is to have lot sizes ranging from 657 to 661 square meters in size. And just for those like myself that prefer standard measurements, that's less than a hundred square feet of reduction that's been requested. So the minor variance is intended to assist with a future land division application to divide the property in two. There is a map at the back of the report chair. It's attachment one. It shows the proposed lot division with lot B and lot A. Lot B would be the severed parcel and lot A would be the retained parcel. In terms of looking at the development, the official plan designates the property as settlement area, which is the appropriate location to direct development towards. The official plan goes to quite length directing development to the settlement areas. In terms of the compliance with the zoning, the request today with this application is a modest reduction in the 665 square meter lot size. All other provisions of the zoning bylaw will be complied with, although there is another application to be considered. In terms of correspondence, we have received some comments. We've got one from Daria Sengona Govani, and I apologize for the pronunciation of that name, who's indicated that she's concerned with the yard reductions, both the interior and the side yard. This application isn't dealing with those, so I'm going to reserve Daria's comments for the next application, if I may, Chair. There was also a correspondence from the town of Smith Falls. They were clarifying the scale of development and they were confirmed through the lawyer for the applicant who's with us today that the development proposed is for a single detached dwelling on each lot with a detached garage. So again, to confirm, there is to be a house, a single detached house with a detached garage proposed for each lot, and that is the focus of the development. Mr. Chair, I've gone through the applications. I've assessed them against the four conditions that are set out, the four tests that are set out in the Ontario Planning Act for Committee of Adjustment applications. The first test is whether the application maintains the intent and purpose of the official plan, and I believe, as I stated earlier, that residential development is encouraged to be in settlement areas such as this, and this application maintains that intent. With respect to the zoning by-law, it's the intent of the minimum lot size to be consistent with the lot fabric, to establish a consistent sort of lot fabric within the neighborhood. The proposed lot areas for the severed and retained lots are very, very close to the minimum set out in the by-law, and I would submit that it would be very difficult to visually distinguish a lot that's 7,200 square feet in size versus 7,100 square feet in size. And in my opinion, this development does maintain the intent and purpose of the zoning by-law. The next test is whether it's desirable for the appropriate development and use of the land. I think everything in planning today is looking at infill and intensification, and that this development would fit that bill and would be seen as an appropriate and desirable form of development for the subject lands. The final test, Mr. Chair, as you know, is whether the application is minor, and minor is not a question of mathematical formula, it's a question of effect. Will this minor variance have a minor effect on the surrounding neighborhood? And again, I think that the reduction that's being asked today personifies the concept of minor, and that there will be no impact on the neighborhood as a result of the reduction in the minimum lot size requested with this application. That being said, Mr. Chair, I'm satisfied as a professional planner in the province of Ontario, that the application meets the four tests set out in the Planning Act for Committee of Adjustment decisions. There are no conditions that I'm recommending with this application, and my recommendation to the committee today is that the application that's been submitted, that is, I'm sorry, that it's A21-005, Perot Minor Variance, be granted as submitted to you. I'm happy to answer any questions if you have any. Chair.

speaker: forbess
text: And if you want to address Forbes, please. Thank you, Chair. So I'm not going to repeat my assessment of the property, though this application was submitted to request two specific variances. One was to reduce the minimum side yard setback for the dwelling from three meters to 1.5 meters. That's going from 10 feet down to five feet. And as well requesting the rear yard setback from three meters to 1.5 meters. Mr. Chair, I did have an opportunity to review this application with Mr. Andrew Howard, the agent for the applicant, to seek clarification. The request for reduction in the rear yard setback, Mr. Chair, I do not believe is necessary. It was submitted only to deal with the detached garage. And the detached garage is permitted under the current zoning of the property to be one meter from the lot line. They're proposing 1.5 meters. And therefore the second component of the request is redundant and will not be part of the recommended decision today. The only question that this application needs to address, Mr. Chair, is the side yard setback reduction from three meters down to 1.5 meters. When you look at side yard setbacks, Mr. Chair, they're designed and intended to establish a sense of yard space and separation between buildings on a property. And in reviewing the proposal with Mr. Howard, we've come to an agreement that the best thing would be to have the 1.5 meter lot lines abutting each other that the house on the west side of the lot has a westerly side yard of three meters and an easterly side yard of 1.5 meters. And that the easterly lot would have a lot, side yard setback on the west of 1.5 meters and on the east of three meters. This wouldn't mean, Mr. Chair, that there would be 1.5 meters between the two new lot line of the two dwellings, but where they abut existing development to the east and the west, they would maintain the three meter side yard setback. And I think that that would be a much better configuration than each of the lots having an easterly side yard setback of 1.5 meters. My assessment of the applications is that the official plan is maintained by this application. The intent of the zoning bylaw is maintained. Albeit with this change and that it is desirable for the use of the land and it is seen as being minor in nature. But with respect to the comments that we received from the abutting property owners, I think that the redesign, having three meters on the outside of the property and 1.5 meters on the inside of the properties will respect the interests of the abutting property owners. And so the condition that's written before the committee, I believe is not correct, Mr. Chair. I would like that condition to be rewritten and read as follows. That the applicant provide a revised site plan for the development of the two proposed lots, which has a 1.5 meter side yard on the east side of lot B and the west side of lot A proposed so that there is a three meter side yard against abutting lands. I've emailed that to Christy and that's my report, Mr. Chair. And I see Mr. Howard has a question. So that's my report as it stands right now, Mr. Chair. Thank you. Go ahead, Mr. Howard.

And they're extremely effective and they do not create problems between properties. This is a little different situation in this respect, but I think that the important thing to realize, Mr. Chair, is that this 1.5, although it's recognized as a standard, it would be the two new houses that would be dealing with this reduction and not abutting properties.
